title: Changelog summarizer (smoke test)
summary: A $0 demo that turns a pasted changelog into three plain-English customer bullets, using free AI models with a recorded fallback.

nodes.label: Visitor's browser
nodes.does: Loads the single-page app, sends a pasted changelog to the API and shows the three-bullet summary, or a recorded run when the live AI quota is used up.
nodes.why: The page is static assets served by the Worker, so it costs no Worker CPU. The Startup name, colors and problem come from project.json, so a new Project changes data, not layout.

nodes.label: Worker API (Hono)
nodes.does: Serves /api/ask and /health. It validates the changelog text, adds the three-bullet system prompt, keys the visitor by a peppered hash, and hands the call to llm().
nodes.why: One Worker holds every key and the database URL, so nothing secret ever reaches the browser. /health always answers 200 with {ok, db, sha} so the Pages front and the deploy smoke check can read why it is not ok.

nodes.label: Summary prompt
nodes.does: A fixed system prompt tells the model to reply with exactly three plain-English bullets for customers and to treat the pasted changelog as content, not instructions.
nodes.why: The whole product is this one instruction, so it lives next to the route and has a test that checks it reaches the model.

nodes.label: llm(): free model chain
nodes.does: Counts the call against a daily cap in Neon, then tries Workers AI, Groq and OpenRouter free tiers in order, and falls back to a recorded run with a banner.
nodes.why: Every model call goes through one function, so the $0 rule holds in one place: no database or a full day fails closed to demo mode instead of spending.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres
nodes.does: Stores the daily call counter, the recorded demo runs and visitor submissions, one Neon project per Project.
nodes.why: Row-level security keys visitor rows on app.visitor, and the Worker connects as an app role that cannot bypass it. HTTP queries fit the Worker's short requests.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages front
nodes.does: The link to share. It sends visitors to the live Worker when /health answers, and shows the recorded runs when it does not.
nodes.why: A free Worker or database can sleep or be retired; the Pages link and its recorded runs stay up, so an old link never shows an error.

nodes.label: ship.yml: build, publish, deploy
nodes.does: Build runs the Claude Code agent with a read-only token. Publish, on a fresh runner, refuses protected-path changes, tests, builds and runs gitleaks before pushing. Deploy checks the review, placeholders, Pages and database size, then ships the Worker with its secrets and publishes Pages.
nodes.why: Heavy work runs in GitHub Actions, never on a laptop, and the agent that writes the code never holds a deploy secret or a push token.

nodes.label: This explainer and the clip
nodes.does: The project-explainer skill writes public/explainer.json; a script checks it and builds this page. A best-effort job turns the same facts into a short how-it-works video.
nodes.why: One fixed page format for every Project, readable from a file with no server, so each Project can be understood in about three minutes.

tour.title: Paste a changelog, press Summarize.
tour.say: The visitor pastes up to 2000 characters of changelog into the React page and posts it to the API.

tour.title: One Worker holds every key.
tour.say: The Hono API validates the prompt and keys the visitor by a peppered hash; secrets and the database URL never leave the Worker.

tour.title: One instruction shapes the answer.
tour.say: The Worker adds a system prompt that asks for exactly three plain-English customer bullets.

tour.title: Free models, then a recorded run.
tour.say: llm() counts the call against a daily cap, tries Workers AI, Groq and OpenRouter free tiers, and falls back to a recorded run with a banner, so it stays at zero dollars.

tour.title: Its own database, locked per visitor.
tour.say: Each Project gets its own Neon database; row-level security keeps each visitor's rows to themselves.

tour.title: A stable link with recorded runs.
tour.say: The GitHub Pages front shows the recorded summaries when the live Worker is asleep.
